meta.scope: Peru batch 3 — Lima Metropolitana, departmental poverty contrast, trade agreements (Pacific Alliance), education/health, and fiscal anchors (MEF budget). Completes the homogeneity check.
meta.homogeneity_note: Same national ENAHO framework. Sierra and Selva rural + high-poverty departments (Cajamarca, Loreto, Puno) carry the highest rates; Costa and mining departments such as Ica/Moquegua are far lower.

candidates.title: Lima Metropolitana — capital statistical identity
candidates.description: Capital metropolitan area and largest urban economy. Primary high-frequency domain for ENAHO, EPEN and many price/activity series. Intermediate monetary-poverty incidence relative to the national average.
candidates.notes: Dominant metro node. 2025 monetary poverty in Lima Metropolitana ~27.3% (close to the national 25.7%). Continuously published as a distinct geographic domain in poverty and living-conditions reports.

candidates.title: Departamento de Cajamarca — highest-poverty contrast
candidates.description: Andean department with the highest monetary-poverty incidence in the 2025 results. Tests the statistical hierarchy under persistent high poverty despite mining presence.
candidates.notes: Poverty-contrast department. 2025 monetary poverty 41.0% (highest); also among the highest in extreme poverty. Has remained in the top poverty group for many consecutive years.

candidates.title: Departamento de Loreto — high-poverty Selva contrast
candidates.description: Amazonian department with the second-highest monetary-poverty incidence. Completes the periphery contrast alongside Cajamarca and Puno.
candidates.notes: 2025 monetary poverty 40.1%. Illustrates the Selva high-poverty cluster under a common national measurement framework.

candidates.title: Departamento de Puno — high-poverty Sierra contrast
candidates.description: Southern Andean department ranking among the highest in monetary and extreme poverty.
candidates.notes: 2025 monetary poverty 37.5%. Part of the persistent high-poverty Sierra group.

candidates.title: Departamento de Ica — low-poverty contrast
candidates.description: Coastal department with the lowest monetary-poverty incidence in the 2025 results.
candidates.notes: 2025 monetary poverty 4.5% — lowest of the departments. Completes the low-poverty pole opposite Cajamarca/Loreto/Puno.

candidates.title: Pobreza monetaria por departamento (INEI)
candidates.description: Official departmental tabulations of monetary poverty and extreme poverty. Primary source for the inter-departmental poverty gradient.
candidates.notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2025 ranking (selected): Cajamarca 41.0%, Loreto 40.1%, Puno 37.5%, … Ica 4.5%, Madre de Dios 7.3%, Moquegua 7.8%. National average 25.7%.

candidates.title: Alianza del Pacífico (Protocolo Comercial)
candidates.publisher: Estados miembros de la Alianza del Pacífico (Chile, Colombia, México, Perú)
candidates.description: Regional integration initiative and commercial protocol among the four Pacific-facing Latin American economies. Preferential trade, investment and regulatory cooperation framework.
referenced_by: Peruvian trade-agreement monitoring and MinCETUR reports
Export and import statistics with AP partners
candidates.notes: Latin American Pacific counterpart to MERCOSUR. Continuously cited in official trade reporting.

candidates.title: Presupuesto del Sector Público / National Budget (MEF)
candidates.description: Annual public-sector budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues and expenditure of the central government and transfers.
candidates.notes: Operational fiscal framework. 2026 budget ~S/ 257.6 bn. Education, health, transport and security absorb a large share of the functional allocation.

candidates.title: Estadísticas de educación / Education statistics & budget
candidates.description: Enrolment, attainment and learning-outcome indicators together with the education functional budget. Complements ENAHO education modules.
candidates.notes: Education is a major budget priority. ENAHO provides household-side attainment and access data; administrative systems and learning assessments supply the supply-side picture.

candidates.title: Estadísticas de salud / Health coverage & expenditure
candidates.publisher: Ministerio de Salud / SIS / INEI / MEF
candidates.description: Health-insurance coverage (SIS and other schemes), health-service access and the health functional budget. Complements ENAHO health modules.
candidates.notes: Health is a major and growing budget function. SIS (Seguro Integral de Salud) is the principal public insurer for the uninsured population; ENAHO tracks affiliation and access.

proposed_edges.basis: Departmental poverty tables are geographic disaggregations of the national monetary-poverty measurement.
Cajamarca’s high poverty ranking is derived from the departmental poverty tabulations.
Lima Metropolitana is a primary geographic domain of the ENAHO.
Pacific Alliance preferential trade is a recurring analytical dimension of merchandise-trade reporting.
Education is a major functional allocation in the national budget.
Health is a major functional allocation in the national budget.
ENAHO provides household-side health affiliation and access indicators.
